section: Evolution of Panchayati Raj - Community Development Programme, Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta, G.V.K. Rao and L.M. Singhvi committees
subsections: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject

accepted.s: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was appointed in which year?
accepted.x: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was appointed in January 1957 and submitted its report in November 1957.
accepted.tq: Use the precise year rather than the year of the subsequent implementation of Panchayati Raj.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was appointed by the Government of India during the tenure of which Prime Minister?
accepted.x: The committee was appointed by the Government of India during the Nehru era to review the Community Development Programme and National Extension Service.
accepted.tq: Identify the government and political period associated with the committee.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal mandate of the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was to review the working of which programmes?
accepted.x: The committee reviewed the Community Development Programme of 1952 and the National Extension Service of 1953.
accepted.tq: Match the committee with the specific programmes it was asked to review.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following expressions is most closely associated with the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee?
accepted.x: Democratic decentralisation was the central idea associated with the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee, along with the recommendation of a three-tier system.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related committee slogans and subjects.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Ashok Mehta Committee was appointed by which government?
accepted.x: The Ashok Mehta Committee was appointed in December 1977 by the Janata Government and submitted its report in August 1978.
accepted.tq: Use the appointing government as the decisive clue in a committee question.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Ashok Mehta Committee:
1. It was appointed in 1977.
2. It submitted its report in 1978.
3. It made 132 recommendations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Ashok Mehta Committee was appointed in December 1977, submitted its report in August 1978, and made 132 recommendations.
accepted.tq: Verify the appointment year, report year and numerical detail separately.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The basic institutional model recommended by the Ashok Mehta Committee consisted of:
o: Four tiers including the Nyaya Panchayat
Three tiers headed by the Zila Parishad
Two tiers, including the Mandal Panchayat
accepted.x: The Ashok Mehta Committee recommended a two-tier Panchayati Raj structure, including the Mandal Panchayat, for the revival of Panchayati Raj Institutions.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two-tier Ashok Mehta model from the three-tier Balwant Rai Mehta model.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following committees was concerned with block-level planning?
accepted.x: The Dantwala Committee, appointed in 1978, dealt with block-level planning.
accepted.tq: Match the planning level with the committee specifically associated with it.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Hanumantha Rao Committee is associated with:
accepted.x: The Hanumantha Rao Committee of 1984 submitted a report on district planning.
accepted.tq: Use the planning-level distinction: Dantwala for blocks and Hanumantha Rao for districts.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the role of the Collector in the recommendations associated with Hanumantha Rao?
o: The Collector was to retain the central coordinating role.
The Collector was to be abolished as a district authority.
The Collector was to function only as a judicial officer.
The Collector was to be replaced by the Gram Sabha.
accepted.x: The Hanumantha Rao approach to district planning retained the Collector in the central coordinating role.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority retains the coordinating responsibility in the stated institutional arrangement.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The G.V.K. Rao Committee was appointed by the:
accepted.x: The G.V.K. Rao Committee was appointed by the Planning Commission in 1985.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who appointed the committee?’ test to distinguish constitutional and planning bodies.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The G.V.K. Rao Committee dealt primarily with:
o: Administrative arrangements for rural development and poverty alleviation programmes
Election disputes of urban local bodies
accepted.x: The full title associated with the G.V.K. Rao Committee was ‘Administrative Arrangements for Rural Development and Poverty Alleviation Programmes’.
accepted.tq: Match the committee with its distinctive official subject rather than a general Panchayati Raj theme.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The phrase ‘grass without roots’ was used in the context of Panchayati Raj Institutions by the:
accepted.x: The G.V.K. Rao Committee observed that Panchayati Raj Institutions had become ‘grass without roots’.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive quotation to separate committees with overlapping rural-development concerns.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The L.M. Singhvi Committee was appointed by the Rajiv Gandhi Government in:
accepted.x: The L.M. Singhvi Committee was appointed in 1986 by the Rajiv Gandhi Government to prepare a concept paper on reviving Panchayati Raj Institutions.
accepted.tq: Separate the Singhvi appointment year from the later Thungon and Gadgil committees of 1988.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was the title of the L.M. Singhvi Committee report?
o: Working Group on Panchayats and Cooperatives
Revitalisation of Panchayati Raj Institutions for Democracy and Development
accepted.x: The L.M. Singhvi Committee was associated with the title ‘Revitalisation of Panchayati Raj Institutions for Democracy and Development’.
accepted.tq: Match the exact title with the committee instead of relying on a broad subject similarity.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation associated with the L.M. Singhvi Committee?
o: Abolition of the Gram Sabha as an institution of direct democracy
Regular, free and fair elections to Panchayati Raj Institutions
Constitutional recognition of Panchayati Raj Institutions
Nyaya Panchayats for clusters of villages
accepted.x: The Singhvi Committee supported the Gram Sabha as the embodiment of direct democracy; it did not recommend its abolition. It also supported constitutional recognition, regular elections and Nyaya Panchayats for clusters of villages.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses a stated recommendation while the other three retain the committee’s approach.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Thungon Committee was associated with which of the following combinations?
o: 1988; constitutional recognition, three tiers and five-year term
accepted.x: The Thungon Committee of 1988 dealt with constitutional recognition, a three-tier structure and a five-year term for Panchayati Raj Institutions.
accepted.tq: Match the committee with its year and cluster of recommendations, not merely its general subject.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Thungon Committee was a sub-committee of the:
accepted.x: The Thungon Committee was constituted as a sub-committee of Parliament’s Consultative Committee.
accepted.tq: Identify the parent institutional body rather than the committee’s recommendation.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Gadgil Committee was constituted by the:
o: Congress Party Committee on Policy and Programmes
accepted.x: The Gadgil Committee was constituted by the Congress Party Committee on Policy and Programmes in 1988.
accepted.tq: Use the exact appointing body to distinguish Gadgil from Thungon, which had a parliamentary connection.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following was associated with the Gadgil Committee?
1. Constitutional status for Panchayati Raj Institutions
2. Direct elections
3. Reservations
4. Model for the 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Gadgil Committee was associated with constitutional status, direct elections, reservations and the model for the 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of related recommendations together; the complete combination is supported.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which committee was concerned with the rationalisation of Panchayat statistics?
accepted.x: The V.R. Rao Committee of 1960 dealt with the rationalisation of Panchayat statistics.
accepted.tq: Distinguish statistics from audit, budgeting and training subjects among specialist panels.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The S.D. Mishra Committee was associated with the:
o: Working Group on Panchayats and Cooperatives
accepted.x: The S.D. Mishra Committee of 1961 was the Working Group on Panchayats and Cooperatives.
accepted.tq: Match the specialist committee with its exact working-group subject.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following committees was concerned with Panchayati Raj administration?
accepted.x: The Vishwa Raman Committee of 1961 dealt with Panchayati Raj administration.
accepted.tq: Separate the general administrative study from the specialist studies of Nyaya Panchayats, Gram Sabha and finances.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: G.R. Rajagopalan Committee is correctly associated with:
accepted.x: The G.R. Rajagopalan Committee of 1962 dealt with Nyaya Panchayats.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional keyword to distinguish Nyaya Panchayats from Gram Sabha and election studies.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The R.R. Diwakar Committee examined the subject of:
accepted.x: The R.R. Diwakar Committee of 1963 was associated with the Gram Sabha.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between Gram Sabha and Panchayat finance committees by their specific subjects.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about K. Santhanam:
1. He was associated with Panchayati Raj finances in 1963.
2. He was associated with Panchayati Raj elections in 1965.
3. He was associated with audit and accounts in 1966.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: K. Santhanam was associated with Panchayati Raj finances in 1963 and Panchayati Raj elections in 1965. Audit and accounts in 1966 was associated with R.K. Khanna.
accepted.tq: Check the two different years and reject the statement that assigns another committee’s subject to Santhanam.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: G.R. Rajagopalan was associated with Nyaya Panchayats, not Panchayat elections. K. Santhanam was associated with Panchayat elections in 1965.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped subject by comparing specialist panels with their narrowly defined functions.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The committee associated with training centres for Panchayati Raj was the:
accepted.x: The G. Ramachandran Committee of 1969 dealt with training centres. A.S. Trivedi is not the committee associated with this subject in the given classification.
accepted.tq: Resolve the look-alike distractor by matching the exact subject with the correct committee name.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs correctly represents the years associated with K. Santhanam’s two Panchayati Raj studies?
accepted.x: K. Santhanam dealt with Panchayati Raj finances in 1963 and Panchayati Raj elections in 1965.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two closely related subjects and their non-consecutive years.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following committees in chronological order of their appointment or constitution:
A. Dantwala Committee
B. Balwant Rai Mehta Committee
C. G.V.K. Rao Committee
D. Ashok Mehta Committee
accepted.x: The correct order is Balwant Rai Mehta (1957), Dantwala (1978), Ashok Mehta (1977–78), and G.V.K. Rao (1985). Since the Ashok Mehta Committee was appointed in December 1977, the precise order is Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta, Dantwala, G.V.K. Rao; therefore option b is not correct as written.
accepted.tq: Check the exact years before ordering, especially where two committees fall close together.
accepted.sec: Committees → year, government, chronological order, subject  [APPSC]
